newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba terms acquittal in hijacking case 'manipulation'.
newsitem.headline: Cuba terms acquittal in hijacking case 'manipulation'.

text.p: The Cuban government on Thursday described the acquittal in the United States of a Cuban accused of hijacking a Cuban domestic flight to the U.S. naval base at Guantanamo Bay a year ago as an example of U.S. "political manipulation".

Former Interior Ministry officer Jose Fernandez Pupo was declared not guilty of air piracy by a court in Washington on May 29. He had been charged with seizing control of a small passenger plane at gunpoint and forcing it to land at the Guantanamo Bay base, on the southeast tip of the island, last July.

"We know the amount of political manipulation that goes into the treatment of such issues in the United States," Foreign Ministry spokesman Miguel Alfonso told a regular weekly news briefing when asked about the court decision.

"What has happened (this acquittal) provides one more proof of who principally impels and condones terrorism," he added. He suggested that Washington's political hostility toward the communist-ruled island pervaded even the judicial system.
After the hijacking last July, Cuba demanded that Fernandez Pupo be extradited to Cuba to be tried.

U.S. newspaper reports said last week that Fernandez Pupo remained in detention following his acquittal, pending a U.S. Immigration and Naturalisation Service decision on whether he should be extradited or given political asylum.

Havana has argued since the hijacking that Fernandez Pupo's extradition to Cuba would be in line with a May 1995 migration agreement with the United States, under which Washington undertook to repatriate Cubans trying to emigrate illegally to the United States.
Under the accord, both sides also agreed to oppose acts of violence associated with the illegal emigration by Cubans.

In response to a question, Alfonso said he did not rule out Cuba raising the issue of Fernandez Pupo at forthcoming talks on migration issues with the United States, expected to take place in early July.

The talks will be the latest in periodic discussions Cuba and the United States have held to review implementation of their migration accords of May 1995 and September 1994 -- which were aimed at halting a flow of Cuban boat people toward Florida.
The last such talks were held in Havana in December 1996. So far, the venues have rotated for the talks, so the July talks would be expected to take place in New York.
